## **I. Academic Foundations: The Fallacy of Undifferentiated Frame-Change EIG**

### **1\. Thermodynamic Analysis of the Zero-Score Empirical Result**

The telemetry from production\_run\_1784964670 demonstrates that while P0 eliminated internal tautology and prevented EFE numerical explosions, it encountered a fundamental information-theoretic bottleneck: **Entropic Equivalence**.

Under the active inference framework, Expected Information Gain (EIG) over a binary indicator ![][image1] measures the reduction in uncertainty regarding whether an action induces *any* state transition. However, in interactive environments:

![][image2]An un-directed action (such as opening a menu, toggling a palette, or executing an invalid cursor step) alters the observable boundary pixels ![][image3], producing ![][image4]. Consequently:

![][image5]The Beta posteriors for all executable actions increment their ![][image6] parameters at identical rates. The EIG term ![][image7] collapses back to isotropic exploration because the system cannot distinguish **task-relevant work** from **incidental state dissipation**.

## **II. Technical Deep Dive: Refinement to Discriminative Task-Relevant EIG (P0.5)**

To convert EIG from an un-directed entropy-seeking term into a discriminative task-progress vector, we must scale posterior updates by normalized grid-state displacement ![][image8].

  Observation Frame (X\_t) ───► Grid Distance Metric ───► Δd\_task \= d(X\_t, X\_t-1)  
                                                                 │  
                                                                 ▼  
  Beta Update Gating ◄─── Is Δd\_task Task-Relevant? ◄─── Weighted Alpha Increment  
          │  
          ▼  
  Discriminative EIG Score: G'(a) \= G\_base(a) \- w\_EIG \* I\_a^task \- w\_task \* R\_task
